desc: AC2 of #13141. Nova must recognise requests to view or download a Progress Snapshot as one ViewChildProgressSnapshot intent and hand the request to the Eduscope agent. Add a claimed flow in pxp-ai that: - Subclasses Flow directly and carries the twelve AC2 utterances in its class docstring, which is what the router uses as the intent description. Include negative clauses against the four sibling flows for reading progress, speaking progress, assignment results and assignment rubrics, since those name specific reports while these rows name progress with no qualifier. - Treats a download request as the same intent, per AC2.1. - Claims the endpoint handle "eduscope". This is a different remote from "team-tracker" despite earlier notes in the repo saying otherwise. Until this story the Eduscope URL carried no handle and was card-routed through a generated agent. - Resolves the child through the shared selection component from #16892 before dialling, then dials with the parent's original utterance rather than their answer to the selection card. - Registers with its own failure message, capability hint and state namespace, and bumps the agent-count pins. Out of scope: AC4 timeframe rules, AC5 through AC9. Known gap to track separately: the resolved child is not forwarded to the remote, so a parent with several children is asked which one twice. AC2 asks for the detected entities to be passed on. Closing it means amending the architecture decision that currently keeps the entity on our side. Deployment dependency: the "eduscope=" handle must be added to the A2A_AGENT_ENDPOINTS variable in each environment's Azure DevOps variable group. Without it the flow answers as unavailable. Done when: - All twelve AC2 utterances route to this agent with no ambiguity, verified by running its routing table together with the four sibling tables against a live model. - The unit suite passes with the updated agent-count pins.

title: Optimize for ocr
desc: ## OCR pipeline — how it works Azure Content Understanding does the reading. This service is the machinery around it: staging, queuing, normalising and correcting. **Asynchronous by design.** A multi-page PDF outlives any HTTP timeout, and an ingress will cut a long request regardless — so submission returns `202` with a job id and callers poll. There is no synchronous path. **The engine is a port, not a vendor.** Adapters implement `describe()` / `availability()` / `analyze()` and register by name; `GET /v1/engines` publishes the catalogue. Nothing above the port knows Azure exists — the domain model carries no vendor types. Two adapters exist today: | Engine | Analyzer | Use for | | --- | --- | --- | | `azure-cu-read` | `prebuilt-read` | text only — cheaper, better for handwriting | | `azure-cu-layout` | `prebuilt-layout` | plus tables, formulas, selection marks | ### Correction is the accuracy lever `llm-fix` sends Azure OpenAI the text plus the words the engine itself scored low, and receives an **edit list**, not a rewritten document. Each edit quotes ~24 characters of surrounding context; an edit that cannot be located exactly in the source is rejected rather than guessed at, so a hallucinated fix fails to apply instead of silently corrupting the transcript. **Measured: 2.35% → 1.15% CER, a 51% relative reduction.** It was already implemented and unverified until this work. Enabling it is a real accuracy gain. ### Accuracy can now be measured `ocr_service.evaluation.metrics` (CER/WER) and `scripts/evaluate.py` score an engine and an optional correction pass over a corpus, caching responses so re-runs are free. The browser UI scores a single dropped page live against a `.txt` and shows a word-level diff. Before this, the service could produce output at any scale with no way to say whether it was right. ### Operational note A worker must consume the queue. `ROLE=api` serves routes and consumes nothing, so a job submitted to it stays `pending` forever. Use `ROLE=both`, or run a separate `ROLE=worker` process. ### Not claimed The IAM corpus accuracy figure is **withdrawn**. The form-splitting step places its boundary wrong often enough that ~17.6% of reported errors were the harness rather than the engine. `--split-handwriting` is marked experimental, and no corpus figure produced with it is quotable as engine accuracy. ### Outstanding - Solve the splitter boundary (needs repeat detection, not a single split point) - Pin the corpus to a commit SHA — it currently tracks a moving branch - The browser holds a second copy of the metrics, held in step by a differential test

title: IOC - Database design
desc: **1. Current recommendation** ------------------------- | Topic | Decision | | --- | --- | | **Database product** | **PostgreSQL 18** — one relational database for governance, operations, and telemetry | | **Version pinning** | Pin a specific **18.x** minor per release bundle — not a floating `latest` tag | | **Time-series extension** | **Not at launch** — add **TimescaleDB** inside PostgreSQL only if triggers S1, S2, or S3 fire | * * * **2. Fleet model** -------------- | Profile | Sites | Devices/site | Total devices | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Small | 1 | 6 | 6 | | Medium | 10 | 14 | 140 | | Large low | 50 | 30 | 1,500 | | Large mid | 200 | 75 | 15,000 | | Large high | 500 | 150 | 75,000 | “Large enterprise” spans **300 → 15,000 samples/s** at typical rates (50×). Validate against the **pilot** footprint, not the label. * * * **3. Message rates** ---------------- | Stream | Typical | Peak | Role | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Telemetry per device | 0.2/s | 1.0/s | Dominates disk | | Events per site per hour | 100 | 200 | Operational | | Alerts | ~7.5% of events | — | Latency-sensitive | | Heartbeat | ~0.03/s per device | — | Health state | **Ingest** = devices × telemetry rate. Large mid: **3,000/s** typical, **15,000/s** peak. * * * **4. Pre-database shaping** ----------------------- | Mechanism | Reduces HTTP load | Reduces DB rows | | --- | --- | --- | | Batch ~5 s | Yes (~150×) | **No** | | Edge aggregate (cold, 1/60 s) | Yes | **Yes** | Large high after aggregate: **~1,250/s** ingest; **~160 MB** local buffer per 72 h offline (vs ~2 GB raw). Hot metrics (alerts, heartbeat, state) are not aggregated. Cold metrics (environmental, occupancy) may be. This classification sets database row rate — see section 10. * * *

title: Improve the restricted-zone configuration UI/UX and fix related bugs
desc: The zone editor (ZoneEditor.tsx, zones.ts) lets an operator: draw polygons on the live preview close a shape with a double-click or Enter undo the last corner drag corners, or move them with the arrow keys apply the changes, then save them It refuses zones the node would reject: fewer than 3 or more than 32 corners, a corner outside the frame, or duplicate consecutive corners. Improve the editing experience and fix the bugs found while using it. Known pain points from the guide: The Savant (WHEP) preview shows the boxes only. Saved zones are drawn on the preview only on a CPU node, so on a Jetson the operator cannot see the zones over the live picture. A saved zone edit takes up to 10 s to apply (config cache TTL), with no feedback in the UI. "Apply" closes the editor but nothing is stored until "Save", so it is easy to lose edits. Collect the remaining UI/UX issues and bugs from internal testing, list them in the PR, and fix them.

title: Retire the office-head fight pipeline

title: Offline streaming inference with the engares model
desc: Write a committed script (not a notebook) that runs the engares A3 stream checkpoint over a video, one frame at a time, carrying the model states between frames. It outputs a per-frame fight probability as CSV, and optionally an annotated mp4. Match the reference preprocessing exactly: resize_with_pad to 256×256 and float in [0, 1]. Determine the frame sampling rate the checkpoint was trained with (from movinet_training.ipynb) and document it; the rate matters for streaming. Pin the TF and tf-models-official versions.

title: Implement audio-scoring-service (local)
desc: ​Standalone FastAPI service: receives audio and a reference passage ( multipart/form-data ), scores it with Azure Pronunciation Assessment, and returns neutral scoring data for clients (e.g. the robot app). Spec: docs/scoring-requirements.md . Scope: local only, no deployment. Tasks: Audio normalization: decode in-process with PyAV (bundled libav, format detected from content; headerless PCM rejected) → 16 kHz mono 16-bit (anti-aliased), VAD trim of leading/trailing silence, validation and error codes. Segment aggregation: word-weighted fluency/prosody, completeness recomputed over the whole passage. Reference alignment: EnableMiscue = false, reference_text input (split on whitespace into reference tokens), per-token normalization, jiwer alignment → matched / substituted / omitted + insertions. Response contract: versioned schema, per-token results, timings in ms. Tests: unit tests per spec acceptance criteria; end-to-end with real audio. Acceptance: spec acceptance criteria pass; works in Swagger with real WAV / WebM / M4A; the response covers all metrics the robot currently uses. Dependencies: Azure Speech key.

title: Setup alarm for sensors and raise notifications
desc: Sensors raise alarms when temperature or humidity leaves its range, a battery runs low, or a device stops reporting. The alarms show on the room overview and in ThingsBoard's alarm list, and reach command centers.

title: Raise climate alarms
desc: As a person working in the office, I want an alarm when a room is too hot, too cold, too humid or too dry, so that someone acts before the room becomes uncomfortable. The rules go on the `climate-sensor` profile or any current profiles that also support temperature and humidity (FP300's `presence-sensor`). Any threshold crossing passes the 5-minute mark will raise an alarm.

title: Set hosted VM instance schedule
desc: The hosted Azure VM runs only Monday to Friday, 08:30-18:30 UTC+7 (01:30-11:30 UTC). Outside those hours it is deallocated, which stops compute billing, and it starts itself before office hours with no human step.

title: Decide the VM stop/start mechanism
desc: As the operator of the hosted instance, I want one decided mechanism that deallocates the VM outside of working hour, so that the schedule runs with no human step and no stored secret. Azure's built-in auto-shutdown only stops the VM, so starting it needs a second mechanism.

title: Setup VM shutdown schedule
desc: Since Azure portal only supports a shutdown schedule, this will be setup first while waiting for #1939 to be worked on. VM will be manually turned on when needed. VM turns off automatically at 6:30PM daily if turned on.

title: Multi-profile for one device
desc: Today a ThingsBoard device record has one `device_profile_id`. A device that is more than one kind (for example the FP300: presence and climate) takes the first matching rule in `PROFILE_RULES`. Its profile must also be added by hand to the other kind's dashboard alias (the FP300 in `Climate sensors`). This user story changes ThingsBoard itself so that one device can hold several profiles.

title: Store several profiles per device
desc: As a platform developer, I want a device-to-profile join table next to the existing column, so that a device can hold extra profiles and the database still rejects profiles that do not exist.

title: Apply extra profiles in the server
desc: As a platform user, I want alarm rules and dashboard aliases to see all of a device's profiles, so that a presence-and-climate sensor appears in both kinds of chart with no alias edit. Depends on #1943

title: Show and edit extra profiles in the UI and from the gateway
desc: As a tenant administrator, I want to see and change a device's extra profiles, and the forwarder to set them when a device is created, so that new mixed devices need no manual step. Depends on #1944

title: Establish the adaptive learning core: shared BKT engine, content pipeline, classroom integration
desc: Goal Make per-skill mastery tracing the core of the tutoring experience, and make it one implementation shared by the tutor and the AI classroom rather than something each side reimplements. Two learner models that disagree cannot be reconciled, so the model is extracted once and both consumers run it. Scope Extract the learner model. Bayesian Knowledge Tracing update, problem selection and lesson mastery, as pure functions with no UI or framework attached, consumed by the tutor and by the classroom. Content pipeline. Turn generated lesson material into tutor-ready problems: steps, scaffolded hint pathways, knowledge components and BKT priors. Nothing reaches the question bank without passing schema validation and a reviewer marking it approved. Classroom integration. A generated lesson can hand a learner to scaffolded practice, and the classroom can read back per-knowledge-component mastery to show progress. Out of scope (separate items) Durable server-side learner storage; accounts and parental consent; parent and teacher reporting; misconception taxonomy and error analysis; item difficulty and prerequisite metadata. Acceptance criteria The learner model exists as a single implementation used by both systems, with parity tests demonstrating it agrees with the code it replaces. Generated content is rejected before write if it fails validation, and cannot enter the question bank without reviewer approval. A classroom lesson runs practice end to end and displays per-knowledge-component mastery. Agreement between AI-assigned knowledge components and human labels is measured and reported, on a stated sample, so the assignment quality is evidenced rather than assumed. Notes / known constraints BKT priors ship uniform across all knowledge components, so mastery moves on very few observations. Calibration needs real response data and is not in this task. Item coverage is thin for many knowledge components, which limits how far adaptive selection can vary the next item. Mastery must continue to update only from graded item results, never from conversation with the AI tutor.

title: Apply SonarQube quality gate to grader_agent
desc: Why: The company SonarQube scan of grader-agent failed: 33.3k lines, 38 bugs, 38.5% duplication, 46.5% coverage. Most of that came from the scan's scope, not the code. With no sonar-project.properties, it scanned a build/ copy of src/, the prototype HTML, scripts and tests, and it had no coverage report. Done (branch sonar-prepush-gate, commit 40c0d45): Pre-push hook runs the SonarQube quality gate before every git push. Feature branches are scanned by a local SonarQube in Docker and judged only on new code. sonar-project.properties limits the scan to src and frontend/src. run_coverage.sh produces coverage for Python and frontend. Smoke test checks /healthz on the real entrypoint. CLAUDE.md holds the quality rules and Definition of Done (C0 100% / C1 ≥ 80% on changed lines, code review, smoke test). AGENTS.md is refreshed to match the code. Result with correct scope: 14.1k lines, 1 bug, 0 vulnerabilities, 86.4% coverage, 0% duplication. The gate passes, and it was verified to block on a real violation. Acceptance criteria: PR merged into develop, CI green. Agree with manager how the company Sonar server is re-scanned with the new scope.

title: SonarQube cleanup for va-edge: remove vendored Savant, reproducible scan, fix findings
desc: The va-edge SonarQube project reported 14 Security and 33 Reliability issues (both rated E), 87 unreviewed hotspots and 0% coverage. No one was running the scan regularly, and nothing in the repo recorded how to run it. About half the findings came from the vendored `Savant/` tree, which is scratch code and was already planned for deletion. Scope: - Remove `Savant/` from the repo. The local copy moves to `source_code/Savant`. - Make the scan reproducible, with coverage (`sonar-project.properties` and `scripts/sonar_scan.py`). - Fix real Security and Reliability issues, and the Maintainability issues worth fixing. - Review every remaining finding and hotspot, and record the reason for each.
